name: Start (or re-start) an OAuth flow
description: Start (or re-start) an OAuth flow Start (or re-start) an OAuth flow. GET /api/projects/{project_id}/mcp_server_installations/authorize/
context:
GET /api/projects/{project_id}/mcp_server_installations/authorize/
Start (or re-start) an OAuth flow. Pass ``template_id`` to (re)connect a catalog template, or ``installation_id`` to reconnect an existing custom install using its cached metadata and per-user DCR creds.
Required: project_id (path) — Project ID of the project you're trying to access. To find the ID of the project, make a call to /api/projects/.
Optional: install_source (query) — * `posthog` - posthog * `posthog-code` - posthog-code; installation_id (query); posthog_code_callback_url (query); return_path (query) — In-app path to land back on after the OAuth round-trip. Must be a same-app relative path.; template_id (query)

name: Every tool the caller can currently reach, across all their connections
description: Every tool the caller can currently reach, across all their connections Every tool the caller can currently reach, across all their connections. GET /api/projects/{project_id}/mcp_server_installations/available_tools/
context:
GET /api/projects/{project_id}/mcp_server_installations/available_tools/
Every tool the caller can currently reach, across all their connections. One request instead of one per connection: an agent surface resolving its tool list on each session cannot afford a fan-out. `do_not_use` and removed tools are omitted — an agent should not see what it cannot call — while `needs_approval` tools are listed with their state so the caller can explain the block rather than report the capability as missing.
Required: project_id (path) — Project ID of the project you're trying to access. To find the ID of the project, make a call to /api/projects/.

name: Invoke one tool on a connected MCP server
description: Invoke one tool on a connected MCP server Invoke one tool on a connected MCP server. POST /api/projects/{project_id}/mcp_server_installations/{id}/call_tool/
context:
POST /api/projects/{project_id}/mcp_server_installations/{id}/call_tool/
Invoke one tool on a connected MCP server. The request/response shape is plain REST rather than the JSON-RPC envelope `proxy` speaks, because the caller here is an agent surface (the PostHog MCP's `exec`) that wants one tool result, not an MCP transport of its own.
Required: id (path) — A UUID string identifying this mcp server installation.; project_id (path) — Project ID of the project you're trying to access. To find the ID of the project, make a call to /api/projects/.; body (body)

name: Escalate a personal installation to a team-wide shared one
description: Escalate a personal installation to a team-wide shared one Escalate a personal installation to a team-wide shared one. POST /api/projects/{project_id}/mcp_server_installations/{id}/share/
context:
POST /api/projects/{project_id}/mcp_server_installations/{id}/share/
Escalate a personal installation to a team-wide shared one. Owner-only AND admin-only: sharing exposes the owner's credential to project members, so it carries the same gate as creating a shared install outright. Agents require separate explicit grants.
Required: id (path) — A UUID string identifying this mcp server installation.; project_id (path) — Project ID of the project you're trying to access. To find the ID of the project, make a call to /api/projects/.

name: De-escalate a shared installation back to personal
description: De-escalate a shared installation back to personal De-escalate a shared installation back to personal. POST /api/projects/{project_id}/mcp_server_installations/{id}/unshare/
context:
POST /api/projects/{project_id}/mcp_server_installations/{id}/unshare/
De-escalate a shared installation back to personal. Allowed for the credential owner OR a project admin (the reclaim path for shared credentials). The row always stays owned by the ORIGINAL owner — an admin unsharing someone else's install must not capture their credential.
Required: id (path) — A UUID string identifying this mcp server installation.; project_id (path) — Project ID of the project you're trying to access. To find the ID of the project, make a call to /api/projects/.
